title: Correctness of negation-gate emission
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a_1,[0m\ldots,a_m$ be a list of vertex indices, and let $G$ be a list of Boolean gates such that every gate reads only earlier vertices: gate $i$ reads indices less than $n+i$. Suppose every $a_j<n+|G|$. Then the procedure that appends one negation gate for each listed index returns a gate list and corresponding output indices with the following properties: the new gate list extends $G$, is acyclic, and has length $|G|+m$; there are $m$ distinct output indices, each between $n+|G|$ and strictly less than $n$ plus the new gate-list length. On every Boolean input to the original $n$ vertices, these outputs are the negations of the values at $a_1,[0m\ldots,a_m$ in the original gate list. Each output has depth at most one plus the maximum original depth of the listed vertices (with maximum taken as $0$ for an empty list), and every appended gate is a well-formed negation gate.
hypotheses_covered: The original gate list is acyclic
Each listed index is less than $n$ plus the original gate-list length
